rule: Top-level / file-level code (outside any function or type): the caller is the file's module ID. Languages with a module qualifier use it (Python module, JS/TS module, Lua module, OCaml/Haskell module, Rust module path `crate::a::b`, Groovy `pkg.Script#run`). Languages without one (Ruby, PHP, C, C++, ObjC, Zig file scope) use the file path below the scan root without extension (`lib/devise/rails/routes`). An empty caller or `<global>` is a wrong caller.
notes: Layout: src/ (the scan root) holds a Cargo package, Cargo.toml plus src/*.rs, so module paths are crate-relative. The const and static initializers are outside any function or type, so their caller is the file's module path, crate::config (src/config.rs). They are not fields of a type, so no `implicit` <clinit> edge applies. limit is a scanned free function → bare ID, high. Reading config::MAX in main is not a call; `mod config;` is a declaration.
